blocks.content: Introduced conceptually in the Docker Images module, this topic covers the actual mechanics: naming stages, copying specific artifacts between them, and building just one stage on demand.

Each FROM line can be given a name with AS, turning it into a referenceable stage. A Dockerfile with several FROM ... AS name lines is really several independent build environments living in one file.

blocks.alt: AS gives each stage a name to reference later

blocks.content:
FROM golang:1.22 AS builder
# ...build steps...

FROM alpine AS final
# ...runtime steps...

code.content:
FROM golang:1.22 AS builder
# ...build steps...

FROM alpine AS final
# ...runtime steps...

codes.dockerfile:
FROM golang:1.22 AS builder
# ...build steps...

FROM alpine AS final
# ...runtime steps...

blocks.content: COPY --from=stageName pulls specific files out of an earlier stage into the current one, this is the entire mechanism behind shrinking a final image, only the files you explicitly copy over make it into the final stage, nothing else from the builder stage comes along.

blocks.alt: Only explicitly copied files cross from one stage to the next

blocks.content: You are not limited to building the final stage, --target tells docker build to stop at, and produce, a specific named stage. A common pattern adds a dedicated test stage that CI builds and runs independently of the actual production image.

blocks.alt: --target builds and stops at exactly the stage you name

blocks.content:
docker build --target test -t myapp:test .
docker run myapp:test  # runs the test suite, never ships to prod

code.content:
docker build --target test -t myapp:test .
docker run myapp:test  # runs the test suite, never ships to prod

codes.bash:
docker build --target test -t myapp:test .
docker run myapp:test  # runs the test suite, never ships to prod

blocks.content: A common real-world shape separates dependency installation, the actual build, and the runtime image into three distinct stages, each stage only carrying forward exactly what the next one needs.

blocks.alt: Dependencies, build, and runtime, kept cleanly separate

blocks.content: The size difference this unlocks is exactly what was introduced conceptually earlier: a final image with only the runtime artifact, no compiler, no build cache, no intermediate files ever included.

blocks.alt: The compiler and build tools never reach the final image

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Named stages (FROM ... AS name) and COPY --from= are the actual mechanics behind multi-stage builds, only explicitly copied files cross between stages.
--target lets you build and stop at any named stage, a common use is a dedicated test stage that CI runs independently of the production image.
